headline: Hitler and Stalin's foreign ministers sign a non-aggression pact
detail: Ribbentrop and Molotov sign in Moscow. A secret protocol carves Poland, the Baltic states and Bessarabia into German and Soviet spheres. Moscow denies it exists until 1989.

headline: Parliament passes the Emergency Powers Act in a single day
detail: Recalled from recess, MPs give the British government sweeping powers to rule by regulation for the duration of any war.

headline: Britain and Poland sign a pact of mutual assistance
detail: News of the London treaty, and Mussolini's refusal to fight, make Hitler postpone the invasion he had set for the next morning.

headline: Ration cards come into force across Germany
detail: Days before the first shot, Germans need coupons to buy meat, fats, sugar, milk and other staples.

headline: Poland orders general mobilisation, effective the next day
detail: An earlier call-up was cancelled under British and French pressure not to provoke Berlin. Now call-up posters go up across the country.

headline: SS men stage a fake Polish raid on the Gleiwitz radio station
detail: They broadcast a few words in Polish and leave a murdered Silesian, Franciszek Honiok, as 'evidence'. Hitler will cite such 'attacks' to justify war.

headline: Germany invades Poland; Westerplatte is shelled at 04:45
detail: The old battleship Schleswig-Holstein opens fire on the Polish depot at Danzig. Bombers strike the undefended town of Wieluń. Armies cross from north, west and south.

headline: Operation Pied Piper: Britain evacuates its city children
detail: Labels on coats, gas masks in cardboard boxes: about 1.5 million people, mostly children, leave the cities by train within three days.

headline: Bohr and Wheeler publish their theory of nuclear fission
detail: Their paper in Physical Review explains how a uranium nucleus splits. It appears the morning Germany invades Poland.

headline: Britain and France declare war on Germany
detail: Chamberlain broadcasts at 11:15. France follows at 17:00. Australia and New Zealand declare the same day; Canada will follow on 10 September.

headline: U-30 sinks the liner Athenia without warning
detail: Torpedoed north-west of Ireland hours after Britain's declaration, the Canada-bound liner carried over 1,100 passengers. More than 110 people die. Berlin blames Churchill.

headline: Shooting in Bydgoszcz: ethnic Germans and Poles die
detail: As Polish troops withdraw, fighting with armed local Germans leaves 100-300 German civilians and 40-50 Poles dead. Days later German forces begin mass reprisal executions.

headline: Soviet-Japanese ceasefire ends the fighting at Khalkhin Gol
detail: Agreed in Moscow the day before, the truce ends a summer border war in Mongolia that Zhukov won. Stalin's eastern flank is now quiet.

headline: The Red Army invades Poland from the east
detail: Moscow claims Poland no longer exists. That night the Polish president and government cross into Romania by the bridge at Kuty.

headline: U-29 sinks the carrier HMS Courageous off Ireland
detail: More than 500 men die, including her captain. The Royal Navy withdraws its carriers from submarine hunting.

headline: Heydrich orders Polish Jews concentrated in cities and ruled by councils
detail: His express letter to the Einsatzgruppen commanders orders Jews moved from the countryside to towns near railways and governed by Jewish councils obeying German orders.

headline: Warsaw surrenders after three weeks of siege and bombing
detail: Water and power are gone, thousands of civilians are dead and much of the city is in ruins. The garrison marches into captivity.

headline: Germany and the USSR sign a frontier treaty dividing Poland
detail: Molotov and Ribbentrop redraw the line along the Bug; in exchange for more Polish land Germany cedes Lithuania to the Soviet sphere.

headline: Battle of Kock: Poland's last field army surrenders
detail: General Kleeberg's group, out of ammunition, lays down its arms. The campaign is over, but Poland never formally surrenders.

headline: First Battle of Changsha ends with a Japanese retreat
detail: Counter-attacked from north and south, the Japanese Eleventh Army falls back towards Yueyang. China hails its first major victory since Wuhan fell.

headline: Lithuania accepts Soviet bases and gets back Vilnius
detail: The mutual assistance treaty lets 20,000 Red Army troops into Lithuania. The ancient city, Polish since 1920, is handed over.

headline: Roosevelt is handed Einstein's letter on uranium bombs
detail: Economist Alexander Sachs delivers the warning in person. Roosevelt orders action, and a small Advisory Committee on Uranium meets ten days later.

headline: Chamberlain rejects Hitler's offer of peace on German terms
detail: Answering Hitler's Reichstag speech of 6 October, he tells the Commons that Britain wants deeds, not promises, from Germany.

headline: U-47 slips into Scapa Flow and sinks HMS Royal Oak
detail: Two torpedo salvoes sink the battleship at anchor in minutes. Of her 1,234 men and boys, 835 die.

headline: First German air raid on Britain strikes warships in the Forth
detail: Ju 88 bombers attack cruisers near Rosyth. Auxiliary Air Force Spitfires shoot two of them down.

headline: First deportation of Jews to Nisko leaves Ostrava
detail: Eichmann's trial run: about 900 Jewish men are shipped to a marshy 'reservation' near Lublin. Trains from Vienna and Katowice follow.

headline: Rigged elections in Soviet-occupied eastern Poland
detail: With one list of candidates, new 'assemblies' are chosen to ask for annexation by the Ukrainian and Belarusian Soviet republics.

headline: The General Government is set up; forced labour for Jews
detail: Hans Frank rules occupied central Poland from Kraków. On the same day Jewish men aged 14 to 60 are made liable to forced labour.

headline: Roosevelt signs the 'cash and carry' Neutrality Act
detail: Britain and France may now buy American arms, provided they pay up front and carry them in their own ships.

headline: Sonderaktion Krakau: 183 university teachers arrested
detail: Kraków's professors are summoned to a lecture at the Jagiellonian University and seized. They are sent to Sachsenhausen, where several die.

headline: Georg Elser's bomb in Munich misses Hitler by 13 minutes
detail: The carpenter's bomb, hidden in a pillar of the Bürgerbräukeller, kills eight people. Hitler had left early. Elser is caught at the Swiss border.

headline: Venlo: two British intelligence officers kidnapped at the Dutch border
detail: SD agents posing as anti-Nazi officers snatch Best and Stevens, crippling British spying in Western Europe.

headline: Czech universities shut; nine students executed in Prague
detail: After protests at a student's funeral, the occupiers close all Czech universities and send about 1,200 students to Sachsenhausen.

headline: Jews in occupied Poland ordered to wear Star of David armbands
detail: Hans Frank's decree applies from 1 December to every Jew aged ten and over in the General Government.

headline: Scharnhorst and Gneisenau sink the armed merchant cruiser Rawalpindi
detail: The converted liner fights two battleships south-east of Iceland. Captain Kennedy and most of his crew are killed.

headline: Japanese troops capture Nanning in southern China
detail: The landing in Guangxi cuts a supply road from French Indochina to Chongqing. Bitter fighting for Kunlun Pass follows.

headline: The Soviets stage the shelling of Mainila
detail: Moscow blames Finland for shells that fall on a Soviet border village; it is the pretext for war.

headline: The Soviet Union invades Finland; Helsinki is bombed
detail: The Winter War begins. Finland has few tanks or aircraft against a vast army, but it has snow, forest and skis.

headline: Moscow installs a Finnish puppet government at Terijoki
detail: Otto Kuusinen heads a 'Democratic Republic' in the first captured border town. Almost no Finns recognise it.

headline: Battle of Suomussalmi begins in Finland's frozen forests
detail: Finnish ski troops start cutting road-bound Soviet columns into isolated pockets, which they call motti.

headline: Battle of the River Plate: three cruisers take on the Graf Spee
detail: Exeter, Ajax and Achilles fight the pocket battleship off Uruguay. Exeter is crippled, but the damaged German raider runs for Montevideo.

headline: The League of Nations expels the Soviet Union
detail: It is punishment for the invasion of Finland, and the League's last significant act.

headline: Captain Langsdorff scuttles the Graf Spee off Montevideo
detail: Believing a British fleet is waiting, he takes off most of his crew and blows up his ship in the estuary as vast crowds watch.

headline: Air battle of Heligoland Bight: daylight Wellingtons cut to pieces
detail: German fighters destroy more than half of the bomber force. RAF Bomber Command turns to raiding by night.

headline: Hans Langsdorff shoots himself in Buenos Aires
detail: The Graf Spee's captain dies lying on his ship's old imperial ensign, not the swastika flag.

headline: Wawer massacre: 107 Polish men shot in reprisal
detail: After two German soldiers are killed by criminals in a Warsaw suburb, police seize men from their homes and shoot them overnight. The youngest is fifteen.

headline: Chinese troops retake Kunlun Pass in Guangxi
detail: Du Yuming's 5th Corps, China's only mechanised formation, announces the pass is retaken after two weeks of hard fighting.

headline: Food rationing begins in Britain
detail: Each person may buy four ounces of bacon or ham, four of butter and twelve of sugar a week.

headline: Finns destroy Soviet columns at Suomussalmi and on the Raate road
detail: Two Soviet divisions are shattered in deep snow. Thousands freeze; Finland captures tanks, guns and horses.

headline: Mechelen incident: German invasion plans fall into Belgian hands
detail: A lost Luftwaffe plane lands in Belgium carrying an officer with plans for the western offensive; he fails to burn them all.

headline: Polish codebreakers in France make the first wartime Enigma break
detail: At the PC Bruno station near Paris, Rejewski's team uses perforated Zygalski sheets to read a German message of 28 October 1939.

headline: Gassing of disabled people begins at Grafeneck
detail: Twenty-five men from a Munich asylum are killed in a fake shower room in Württemberg. By December, about 10,000 people die there.

headline: Asama Maru incident: a British cruiser stops a Japanese liner
detail: HMS Liverpool removes 21 German men from the ship about 35 miles off Japan's coast, provoking fury in Tokyo.

headline: Destroyer HMS Exmouth is torpedoed with all hands
detail: Sunk by U-22 off Caithness while escorting a merchant ship, she leaves no survivors.

headline: The 1911 US-Japan commercial treaty lapses
detail: Washington had given notice in July 1939. Trade continues for now, but the Americans can restrict it whenever they choose.

headline: German order creates a ghetto in Łódź
detail: The police chief designates the run-down Bałuty district for the city's Jews; some 160,000 people will be crammed inside.

headline: NKVD begins mass deportation of Polish citizens from eastern Poland
detail: Families of settlers, foresters and officials are loaded into freight cars in deep frost. Polish estimates put the first wave near 140,000.

headline: Germany and the USSR sign a major trade agreement
detail: Soviet oil, grain and metals will flow to Germany, blunting the British blockade. In return Moscow gets machinery, the unfinished cruiser Lützow and warship plans.

headline: The Red Army storms the Mannerheim Line
detail: After ten days of bombardment, Soviet troops breach the line near Lähde on the Karelian Isthmus. Within days the Finns fall back to a second line.

headline: Jews of Stettin deported to the Lublin district
detail: In a night raid, more than 800 men, women and children are taken from their homes and sent east in winter. Most will later die at Bełżec.

headline: 'The Navy's here!' HMS Cossack frees 299 seamen from the Altmark
detail: A British boarding party storms the German supply ship in Norway's Jøssingfjord, freeing merchant sailors captured by the Graf Spee.

headline: Randall and Boot's cavity magnetron runs for the first time
detail: In Birmingham the small copper device produces powerful microwaves, making compact radar for night fighters and escorts possible.

headline: London cheers the crews of Ajax and Exeter
detail: About 760 sailors of the River Plate battle march from Waterloo to lunch at the Guildhall. Churchill attends.

headline: Kamen and Ruben confirm carbon-14 at Berkeley
detail: The radioactive isotope, made in a cyclotron, will become a tracer for photosynthesis and, later, the basis of radiocarbon dating.

headline: Stalin's Politburo approves the shooting of Polish prisoners
detail: Beria's proposal condemns about 22,000 officers, police, priests and officials held since 1939. The killings at Katyn and elsewhere begin in April.

headline: Meat rationing starts in Britain
detail: Unlike bacon and butter, meat is rationed by price: one shilling and tenpence worth per person a week.

headline: Treaty of Moscow ends the Winter War
detail: Finland keeps its independence but gives up the Karelian Isthmus and Vyborg. Over 400,000 Karelians leave their homes rather than live under Soviet rule.

headline: A Scapa Flow air raid kills Britain's first civilian bombing victim
detail: James Isbister, 27, is killed at Bridge of Waithe in Orkney when German bombers attack the fleet anchorage.

headline: Hitler and Mussolini meet at the Brenner Pass
detail: In a railway carriage on the frontier, Mussolini promises Italy will join the war at the right moment.

headline: Paul Reynaud replaces Daladier as French premier
detail: Daladier fell over France's failure to help Finland. Reynaud wins the confidence vote by a single vote.

headline: Britain and France pledge never to make a separate peace
detail: The Supreme War Council in London binds the two allies together, and also approves mining Norwegian waters.

headline: Japan installs Wang Jingwei's collaborationist regime in Nanjing
detail: The former Nationalist leader heads a 'Reorganised National Government'. Chongqing denounces him as a traitor.

headline: NKVD begins the Katyn executions
detail: The first prisoners from the Kozelsk camp are taken to the Katyn forest near Smolensk. By May about 22,000 Poles are shot at Katyn, Kalinin, Kharkov and other sites.

headline: HMS Glowworm rams the cruiser Admiral Hipper and sinks
detail: The lone destroyer meets the German invasion force bound for Norway. Her captain, Gerard Roope, wins a posthumous Victoria Cross.

headline: Germany invades Denmark and Norway
detail: Denmark yields within hours. In Oslofjord the Oscarsborg fortress sinks the cruiser Blücher, buying time for the king, government and gold to escape.

headline: First Battle of Narvik: British destroyers raid the German fleet
detail: Five destroyers attack in snow at dawn, sinking two German destroyers and many merchant ships. Both commanders are killed.

headline: Britain's MAUD Committee meets on the atomic bomb
detail: Spurred by the Frisch-Peierls memorandum, Britain's top physicists begin studying whether a uranium bomb is possible.

headline: Second Battle of Narvik: Warspite leads destroyers up the fjord
detail: All eight remaining German destroyers are sunk or scuttled. Their crews go ashore to fight beside the mountain troops.

headline: Second Soviet mass deportation from eastern Poland
detail: This time the NKVD takes mostly the wives, children and parents of men held in Soviet camps, many already shot. Most go to Kazakhstan.

headline: Allied troops land in Norway at Namsos and Harstad
detail: British and French troops arrive to help the Norwegians, but lack air cover, skis and maps.

headline: Himmler orders a concentration camp built at Oświęcim
detail: Former Polish army barracks near the small town, renamed Auschwitz, are chosen to hold Polish political prisoners.

headline: The Łódź ghetto is sealed
detail: Barbed wire and guards close off 163,777 people. Guards have orders to shoot anyone who tries to leave.

headline: Japan opens the Zaoyang-Yichang offensive in Hubei
detail: Japanese armies push west along the Yangtze to seize Yichang, gateway to Sichuan and the wartime capital.

headline: Germany attacks in the West; Churchill becomes Prime Minister
detail: Paratroops land in the Netherlands and Belgium as panzers roll through the Ardennes. Chamberlain resigns that evening. British troops land in Iceland.

headline: Panzers cross the Meuse; Churchill offers 'blood, toil, tears and sweat'
detail: Guderian's corps breaks through at Sedan as Stukas pound French bunkers. Queen Wilhelmina leaves for London.

headline: Rotterdam's centre is bombed and burns
detail: The raid kills hundreds of civilians and leaves tens of thousands homeless. Threatened with more, the Dutch army capitulates the next day.

headline: Eden calls for Local Defence Volunteers
detail: Within hours of his radio appeal, men queue at police stations to join what will become the Home Guard.

headline: General Zhang Zizhong is killed fighting at Nanguadian
detail: The commander of the 33rd Army Group dies leading his men in Hubei, the most senior Chinese general killed in the war.

headline: German armour reaches the Channel near Abbeville
detail: Ten days into the offensive, the panzer corridor cuts the Allied armies in two. The BEF and French in Belgium are trapped.

headline: At Oxford, penicillin saves four infected mice
detail: Florey's team injects eight mice with lethal streptococci and treats four. By morning only the treated mice are alive.

headline: Operation Dynamo begins at Dunkirk
detail: Destroyers, ferries and small civilian craft start lifting soldiers from the harbour mole and beaches under air attack.

headline: Le Paradis: SS troops murder 97 surrendered British soldiers
detail: Men of the Royal Norfolks are machine-gunned against a barn wall. Two survive under the bodies and later testify.

headline: Belgium capitulates; prisoners massacred at Wormhoudt
detail: King Leopold III surrenders his army. Near Dunkirk, SS men kill about 80 British and French prisoners in a barn.

headline: Operation Dynamo ends: 338,226 men saved from Dunkirk
detail: Thousands of French rearguard troops are left behind. In the Commons Churchill vows: 'we shall fight on the beaches'.

headline: Italy declares war on Britain and France
detail: Mussolini speaks from his Rome balcony. Next day Italian bombers attack Malta, beginning a siege that will last two years.

headline: Japanese forces capture Yichang on the Yangtze
detail: The city becomes an air base from which bombers can reach Chongqing more easily.

headline: German troops enter an undefended Paris
detail: Most Parisians have fled south. A swastika flag is hoisted over the Eiffel Tower.

headline: First transport of Polish prisoners arrives at Auschwitz
detail: 728 Polish political prisoners from Tarnów, among them Catholic priests and Jews, become the camp's first mass transport.

headline: Element 93, neptunium, announced in Physical Review
detail: McMillan and Abelson report the first element heavier than uranium. Its decay hints at another element: plutonium.

headline: The Red Army occupies Lithuania; Latvia and Estonia follow
detail: Faced with ultimatums, the Baltic governments let Soviet troops in. On 17 June they enter Latvia and Estonia.

headline: Troopship Lancastria is bombed off Saint-Nazaire
detail: Packed with evacuating soldiers and civilians, she sinks in minutes. Thousands die, the worst loss in British maritime history. Churchill bans the news.

headline: General de Gaulle broadcasts his appeal from London
detail: On the BBC, an unknown brigadier-general urges French soldiers and engineers to join him. Few hear it that night.

headline: German troops massacre Black French soldiers at Chasselay
detail: Near Lyon, about 50 captured tirailleurs sénégalais are separated from white comrades, machine-gunned and crushed by tanks. Similar killings take place across France.

headline: France signs an armistice at Compiègne
detail: Hitler chooses the railway carriage where Germany signed in 1918. The north and Atlantic coast are occupied; the south stays unoccupied.

headline: The USSR seizes Bessarabia and northern Bukovina from Romania
detail: Romania yields to a Soviet ultimatum without a fight. Thousands of refugees cross the Prut.

headline: German troops occupy the Channel Islands
detail: Guernsey was taken the day before and Jersey now follows; British soil is under German rule for the first time.

headline: The Royal Navy shells the French fleet at Mers-el-Kébir
detail: Fearing the ships will reach Germany, Churchill orders them neutralised. 1,297 French sailors are killed.

headline: Battle of Calabria: British and Italian fleets clash
detail: A hit on the battleship Giulio Cesare at extreme range makes the Italian fleet turn for home.

headline: Battle of Britain begins over Channel convoys
detail: The Luftwaffe starts attacking shipping to draw RAF fighters into combat. In Vichy, parliament votes Pétain full powers.

headline: Hitler orders preparations to invade Britain
detail: Directive No. 16 sets out Operation Sea Lion, an invasion across the Channel once the RAF is beaten.

headline: Britain closes the Burma Road for three months
detail: Under Japanese pressure, London stops war supplies moving from Rangoon to China during the rainy season. Chongqing feels betrayed.

headline: Roosevelt signs the Two-Ocean Navy Act
detail: Congress authorises a 70 per cent increase in the fleet's tonnage, with new carriers, battleships and cruisers.

headline: Puppet Baltic parliaments ask to join the USSR
detail: After single-list elections, assemblies in Tallinn, Riga and Kaunas request annexation; deportations of 'enemies' follow.

headline: Prince Konoe becomes Prime Minister of Japan again
detail: His cabinet, with Matsuoka as foreign minister, moves Japan closer to Germany and toward southern expansion.

headline: Matsuoka proclaims a 'Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere'
detail: Japan's foreign minister announces an Asian order led by Tokyo, eyeing the colonies of defeated France and the Netherlands.

headline: Italy invades British Somaliland
detail: Advancing from Ethiopia, Italian forces outnumber the small garrison, which evacuates by sea from Berbera by 19 August.

headline: Eagle Day: the Luftwaffe turns on RAF airfields
detail: Göring launches his main offensive to destroy Fighter Command in the air and on the ground.

headline: Germany declares a total blockade of the British Isles
detail: Neutral ships in the waters around Britain may now be sunk without warning.

headline: The Hundred Regiments Offensive begins in northern China
detail: Communist Eighth Route Army forces strike railways, bridges and blockhouses across Shanxi and Hebei.

headline: Churchill: never was so much owed by so many to so few
detail: Speaking in the Commons, Churchill honours RAF aircrew at the height of the battle for the skies.

headline: First bombs fall on central London
detail: Off-course German bombers hit the City and the East End during a night raid. Churchill orders Berlin bombed in reply.

headline: RAF bombers raid Berlin for the first time
detail: Damage is slight, but Hitler is enraged and soon redirects the Luftwaffe against London.

headline: Chad declares for de Gaulle and Free France
detail: Félix Éboué, the colony's Guianese-born Black governor, is the first to rally a French territory, followed within days by Cameroon and the Congo.

headline: Second Vienna Award gives northern Transylvania to Hungary
detail: Germany and Italy force Romania to hand over the territory; King Carol abdicates a week later.

headline: Destroyers-for-bases deal between Britain and the United States
detail: Fifty old American destroyers go to the Royal Navy in exchange for 99-year leases on bases from Newfoundland to the Caribbean.

headline: Black Saturday: the London Blitz begins
detail: Some 350 bombers set the docks ablaze in the afternoon and return at night. Over 400 Londoners are killed.

headline: Italy's Tenth Army crosses into Egypt
detail: Graziani's forces take Sollum and advance some 60 miles to Sidi Barrani, then halt and dig in.

headline: Battle of Britain Day: two great raids on London are beaten off
detail: Fighter Command meets both waves at full strength, shattering the Luftwaffe's claim that the RAF is finished.

headline: America's first peacetime draft becomes law
detail: The Selective Training and Service Act requires men aged 21 to 35 to register for military service.

headline: Hitler postpones Operation Sea Lion indefinitely
detail: With air superiority unwon and autumn gales coming, the invasion barges in Channel ports begin to disperse.

headline: U-48 sinks the City of Benares; 77 evacuee children die
detail: The liner, carrying 90 children to Canada, is torpedoed in a gale. Overseas evacuation of children is cancelled.

headline: Tizard Mission shows the Americans the cavity magnetron
detail: British scientists unveil their secret radar valve to US counterparts in Washington. MIT's Radiation Laboratory follows.

headline: Japanese troops move into northern French Indochina
detail: Vichy's officials concede bases; fighting flares at Lang Son. Japan aims to cut supplies to China through Haiphong.

headline: Free French and British forces fail at Dakar
detail: Vichy guns and the battleship Richelieu repel three days of attempts to rally Senegal's capital to de Gaulle.

headline: Washington bans scrap iron and steel exports outside the hemisphere and Britain
detail: The embargo, effective in October, is aimed at Japan, a major buyer of American scrap metal.

headline: Germany, Italy and Japan sign the Tripartite Pact in Berlin
detail: They promise to aid each other if attacked by a power not yet at war, a warning aimed at the United States.

headline: Vichy adopts its first Statute on the Jews
detail: Without German demand, the French state bars Jews from the civil service, the officer corps, teaching, the press and cinema.

headline: Warsaw's Jews are ordered into a ghetto
detail: Loudspeakers announce the decree on Yom Kippur. Jews must move into the designated streets and Poles out within weeks.

headline: Hitler postpones the invasion of Britain until spring
detail: Sea Lion is shelved for the winter; in fact it will never be launched.

headline: Konoe founds the Imperial Rule Assistance Association
detail: Japan's political parties, already dissolved, are replaced by a single mass organisation backing the government and the war.

headline: Princess Elizabeth, 14, makes her first broadcast
detail: On the BBC's Children's Hour she speaks to evacuated children far from home, with her sister Margaret saying goodnight.

headline: Balham Tube disaster: 66 sheltering Londoners die
detail: A bomb bursts the road above Balham station, flooding the platforms with water and earth; a bus tips into the crater.

headline: Draft registration day across the United States
detail: More than 16 million American men sign up for possible military service in a single day.

headline: Britain reopens the Burma Road
detail: Supply trucks roll again from Lashio to Kunming as relations with Japan worsen after the Tripartite Pact.

headline: Jews of Baden and the Saar-Palatinate deported to Gurs
detail: More than 6,500 people, among them the elderly and the sick, are packed onto trains to a Vichy internment camp in the Pyrenees.

headline: Pétain shakes Hitler's hand at Montoire
detail: A day after meeting Franco at Hendaye, Hitler sees the French leader, who soon announces a policy of 'collaboration'.

headline: De Gaulle's Brazzaville Manifesto
detail: Speaking from French Equatorial Africa, he declares Vichy illegitimate and creates an Empire Defence Council.

headline: Italy invades Greece; Metaxas says no
detail: At dawn the Greek leader rejects an Italian ultimatum. Italian troops cross from Albania into the Pindus mountains.

headline: HMS Jervis Bay sacrifices herself to save a convoy
detail: The armed merchant cruiser turns to fight the Admiral Scheer, letting most ships of convoy HX 84 scatter into the dusk.

headline: Roosevelt wins an unprecedented third term
detail: He beats Wendell Willkie, after promising American mothers their sons will not be sent into foreign wars.

headline: Fleet Air Arm Swordfish strike the Italian fleet at Taranto
detail: Twenty-one biplanes from HMS Illustrious cripple three battleships at anchor in one night, a lesson studied closely in Tokyo.

headline: Vichy forces in Gabon surrender to the Free French
detail: The fall of Port-Gentil ends a short civil war; all of French Equatorial Africa now backs de Gaulle.

headline: Molotov arrives in Berlin for talks with Hitler
detail: Two days of meetings, interrupted by an RAF raid, fail to divide the world between them. Hitler turns firmly to war with Russia.

headline: Coventry is devastated in a moonlit raid
detail: Hundreds of bombers hit the city overnight. An estimated 568 people die and the medieval cathedral is left a burnt-out shell.

headline: The Warsaw ghetto is closed off
detail: Some 400,000 Jews are walled into a small area of the city. Official food rations fall far below survival level.

headline: Hungary joins the Tripartite Pact
detail: Romania signs on 23 November and Slovakia on 24 November, drawing central Europe into the Axis.

headline: The Greek army takes Korçë in Albania
detail: Counter-attacking Greek troops push the Italians back over the border, the first major Allied land victory of the war.

headline: Japan formally recognises Wang Jingwei's regime
detail: A basic treaty signed in Nanjing binds the collaborationist government to Japan. Washington promptly announces new loans to Chongqing.

headline: Greek forces take Gjirokastër in southern Albania
detail: The Greeks keep pushing the Italians back through the mountains in winter snow.

headline: Operation Compass: the Western Desert Force attacks
detail: General O'Connor's 36,000 men strike the Italian camps around Sidi Barrani; within days tens of thousands of Italians surrender.

headline: Sheffield Blitz: the steel city is bombed
detail: Raids that night and on 15 December kill hundreds of people and wreck the city centre.

headline: Seaborg's team makes the first plutonium at Berkeley
detail: Bombarding uranium with deuterons in the cyclotron, they create traces of element 94, soon to be named plutonium.

headline: Roosevelt's garden hose: the idea of Lend-Lease
detail: At a press conference he compares lending arms to Britain to lending a neighbour a hose to fight a fire.

headline: Hitler signs Directive 21: Operation Barbarossa
detail: The invasion of the Soviet Union is ordered to be ready by mid-May 1941, to crush Russia in a quick campaign.

headline: Manchester Blitz: two nights of fire
detail: Raids on 22 and 23 December gut the city centre and kill hundreds just before Christmas.

headline: Second Great Fire of London; St Paul's stands
detail: Incendiaries set the City ablaze at low tide. Firefighters save the cathedral, and its dome becomes a symbol of defiance.

headline: Roosevelt: America must be the 'arsenal of democracy'
detail: In a fireside chat he tells Americans that helping Britain is the best way to keep war away from the United States.

headline: Australians take Bardia
detail: In their first battle of the war, the 6th Australian Division storms the fortress port; tens of thousands of Italians surrender.

headline: Roosevelt's Four Freedoms speech
detail: In his annual message he names freedom of speech and worship, and freedom from want and fear, as goals for the whole world.

headline: New Fourth Army Incident in southern Anhui
detail: Nationalist troops ambush the Communist New Fourth Army's headquarters column; thousands are killed or captured. The united front against Japan is badly damaged.

headline: Stukas cripple the carrier Illustrious off Malta
detail: German dive-bombers newly based in Sicily hit her six times. She limps into Grand Harbour, where raids follow her.

headline: The Lend-Lease bill is introduced in Congress
detail: Numbered H.R. 1776, it would let the President lend or lease war supplies to any country whose defence is vital to America.

headline: Free French and the Long Range Desert Group raid Murzuk
detail: After crossing the Libyan Sahara, the patrols attack the Italian fort and airfield. Lieutenant-Colonel d'Ornano is killed.

headline: Battle of Ko Chang: Vichy French ships defeat the Thai navy
detail: In the Franco-Thai war over Indochina's borders, a French squadron sinks Thai warships in the Gulf of Thailand.

headline: Haile Selassie crosses back into Ethiopia
detail: The exiled emperor returns to his country with Gideon Force and Ethiopian patriots, five years after the Italian conquest.

headline: Iron Guard rebellion and pogrom in Bucharest
detail: During three days of revolt against Antonescu, legionnaires murder about 125 Jews and burn synagogues and homes.

headline: Tobruk falls to Australian and British troops
detail: The port is taken in under two days, with about 25,000 Italian prisoners.

headline: Admiral Kimmel takes command of the US Pacific Fleet
detail: The fleet has been based at Pearl Harbor since 1940 as a deterrent to Japan.

headline: Beda Fomm: the Italian Tenth Army surrenders
detail: A British column cuts the coast road after a dash across the desert. In two months O'Connor's force has taken about 130,000 prisoners.

headline: Churchill to America: 'Give us the tools'
detail: In a radio broadcast he tells Roosevelt and the American public that Britain will finish the job if supplied.

headline: Erwin Rommel arrives in Tripoli
detail: He is sent to stop the Italian collapse; the first German troops of what will be the Afrika Korps land two days later.

headline: First patient treated with penicillin at Oxford
detail: Constable Albert Alexander, dying of infection, improves for days on the scarce drug. When supplies run out, he relapses and dies in March.

headline: Swansea's Three Nights' Blitz begins
detail: Over three nights German bombers burn out the heart of the Welsh port town; over 200 people are killed.

headline: Raids in Amsterdam: 425 Jewish men seized
detail: German police round up young men in the Jewish quarter and deport them to Buchenwald and Mauthausen; almost none will return.

headline: Plutonium is identified as a new element
detail: At Berkeley, Arthur Wahl's chemical separation proves element 94 exists. It is kept secret until after the war.

headline: The February Strike: Amsterdam stops work for the Jews
detail: Dockers, tram drivers and factory workers strike in protest at the raids. The Germans crush the strike within two days.

headline: Free French under Leclerc capture Kufra
detail: After a desert siege, the Italian garrison of the Libyan oasis surrenders. Next day Leclerc's men swear to fight until the flag flies over Strasbourg.

headline: Bulgaria joins the Tripartite Pact
detail: German troops begin crossing the Danube into Bulgaria, bound for the Greek frontier.

headline: German decree orders a ghetto in Kraków
detail: Jews must move into the Podgórze district across the Vistula by 20 March; its walls are shaped like gravestones.

headline: Commandos raid the Lofoten Islands
detail: Operation Claymore destroys fish-oil plants in northern Norway; Enigma rotors are seized from the trawler Krebs and 300 Norwegians sail for Britain.

headline: Roosevelt signs the Lend-Lease Act
detail: The United States can now supply Britain, and later China and the USSR, with weapons without payment up front.

headline: Clydebank Blitz
detail: Two nights of bombing destroy or damage nearly every house in the shipbuilding town near Glasgow; over 500 people die.

headline: Two U-boat aces lost in one night
detail: Defending convoy HX 112, HMS Walker and Vanoc sink U-100, killing Schepke, and force Kretschmer's U-99 to surface; he is captured.

headline: Rommel opens his first offensive at El Agheila
detail: Against orders to wait, his small force pushes the thinned British out; within three weeks they are back on the Egyptian border.

headline: Coup in Belgrade overthrows Yugoslavia's pro-Axis government
detail: Two days after the regent signed the Tripartite Pact, officers seize power. Crowds chant 'Better war than the pact'. Hitler orders Yugoslavia destroyed.

headline: Indian and British troops win the Battle of Keren
detail: After eight weeks of fighting in Eritrea's mountains, the Italian stronghold falls; the road to Asmara is open.

headline: Battle of Cape Matapan
detail: Guided by Ultra decrypts, Admiral Cunningham's fleet sinks three Italian heavy cruisers and two destroyers in a night action off Greece.

headline: Rashid Ali seizes power in Iraq
detail: The pro-Axis 'Golden Square' officers drive out the regent, threatening Britain's oil and route to India.

headline: Germany invades Yugoslavia and Greece; Belgrade is bombed
detail: Operation Punishment kills thousands of civilians in the Yugoslav capital. German armies attack from Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary and Austria.

headline: British and Commonwealth troops enter Addis Ababa
detail: Italian forces abandon the Ethiopian capital to troops advancing from Kenya and Somaliland.

headline: Danish envoy signs Greenland's defence over to the United States
detail: Acting without orders from occupied Copenhagen, Henrik Kauffmann lets the Americans build bases on the island.

headline: The 'Independent State of Croatia' is proclaimed
detail: Installed by the Axis, Ante Pavelić's Ustaša regime will murder Serbs, Jews and Roma on a vast scale.

headline: The siege of Tobruk begins
detail: Rommel's troops surround the port, held by the 9th Australian Division. The garrison will hold out for eight months.

headline: Soviet-Japanese Neutrality Pact signed in Moscow
detail: Stalin sees Matsuoka off at the station. Each side can now look elsewhere: Japan south, the Soviet Union west.

headline: The Easter Raid on Belfast
detail: About 200 bombers attack the poorly defended city overnight. Some 900 people are killed, and fire engines rush north from Dublin to help.

headline: Yugoslavia surrenders after eleven days
detail: The country is carved up between Germany, Italy, Hungary, Bulgaria and the new Croatian state; resistance begins in the hills.

headline: British and Commonwealth troops begin evacuating Greece
detail: Over five nights warships take about 50,000 men from beaches and ports; thousands are left behind.

headline: German troops enter Athens
detail: The swastika flag is raised over the Acropolis. The Greek king and government move to Crete.

headline: Anglo-Iraqi War begins at Habbaniya
detail: RAF trainers and old biplanes attack the Iraqi forces besieging their air base west of Baghdad.

headline: Japan attacks the Zhongtiao Mountains in southern Shanxi
detail: Encircling Chinese armies north of the Yellow River, the Japanese inflict one of China's worst defeats of the war.

headline: HMS Bulldog's boarders capture U-110's Enigma secrets
detail: After the U-boat is forced to the surface south-east of Greenland, a boarding party strips her cipher machine and codebooks. She sinks under tow.

headline: Tokyo treaty ends the Franco-Thai War
detail: Under Japanese mediation, Vichy France cedes parts of Laos and Cambodia to Thailand.

headline: London's worst night of the Blitz
detail: Bombers hit the capital under a full moon; 1,436 people die and the Commons chamber is destroyed.

headline: Rudolf Hess flies to Scotland
detail: Hitler's deputy parachutes near Glasgow, hoping to negotiate peace. He is taken prisoner for the rest of the war.

headline: Konrad Zuse demonstrates his Z3 computer in Berlin
detail: The relay machine, run by punched film, is the first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer.

headline: Paris 'green ticket' roundup: 3,710 Jewish men interned
detail: Foreign-born Jews summoned by French police are sent to camps at Pithiviers and Beaune-la-Rolande, the first mass arrest of Jews in France.

headline: Britain's first jet aircraft flies
detail: The Gloster E.28/39, powered by Frank Whittle's engine, makes a 17-minute flight from RAF Cranwell.

headline: German paratroopers invade Crete
detail: Operation Mercury is the first great airborne invasion. Cretan civilians fight alongside British, Australian, New Zealand and Greek troops.

headline: Bismarck sinks HMS Hood; three men survive
detail: In the Denmark Strait a shell detonates the battlecruiser's magazine. She goes down in minutes with 1,415 men.

headline: The Bismarck is sunk in the Atlantic
detail: Her rudder jammed by a Swordfish torpedo, she is battered by British battleships. Over 2,000 men die; little more than a hundred survive.

headline: The Farhud: pogrom against Baghdad's Jews
detail: As Rashid Ali's regime collapses, mobs and soldiers attack Jews during Shavuot. Most counts give about 180 dead; some estimates are far higher.

headline: Clothes rationing begins in Britain
detail: Each person gets 66 coupons a year; a dress costs eleven. Unused margarine coupons serve until clothing books arrive.

headline: Vichy's second Statute on the Jews
detail: It widens job bans and orders a census of Jews in the unoccupied zone; registration lists will later be used for deportations.

headline: Chongqing tunnel disaster during a Japanese raid
detail: Thousands crammed into an air-raid tunnel are suffocated or crushed during hours of bombing; estimates range from under 1,000 to several thousand dead.

headline: Allied and Free French forces invade Vichy Syria and Lebanon
detail: Operation Exporter: Australian, British, Indian and Free French troops cross from Palestine and Transjordan. Frenchmen will fight Frenchmen.

headline: Commandos land at the mouth of the Litani in Lebanon
detail: No. 11 (Scottish) Commando comes ashore a day late after heavy surf. Vichy troops have blown the main bridge; Australians cross by boat and pontoon.
